title: BorgWarner Included in TIME America's Best Companies 2026 List
summary: Read and download our latest press releases.
body_text: Auburn Hills, Michigan, July 10, 2026 – BorgWarner has been awarded on TIME’s list of America’s Best Companies 2026. This prestigious award is presented in collaboration with Statista, the world-leading statistics portal and industry ranking provider. The award list was announced on July 9th, 2026, and can be viewed on TIME.com . TIME and Statista identified America’s Best Companies 2026 based on three primary dimensions: Employee Satisfaction – Based on survey data from ~217,000 verified employees at U.S. companies over the past three years, covering company recommendations and employer ratings across image, atmosphere, working conditions, salary, workplace, and equality. Financial Performance – Drawn from Statista's revenue database (last five years). Companies needed at least US $100 million in revenue in 2025. Performance was assessed on multiple metrics: short-term (2023–2025) and long-term (2021–2025) revenue growth (relative and absolute), changes in net income, asset growth, and the evolution of return on assets (ROA), all for 2023–2025. Sustainability Transparency – Based on an ESG index from Statista's ESG Database and additional research, covering: Environmental: 2024 carbon emissions intensity, reduction rate vs. 2022, and CDP score Social: share of women on the board and existence of a human rights policy Governance: presence of a GRI-aligned CSR report and a compliance/anti-corruption policy The 1,000 highest-scoring companies were recognized as America’s Best Companies 2026. “This recognition from TIME as one of America’s Best Companies reflects the strength of our people, the discipline of our strategy and our commitment to responsible business practices,” said Joseph Fadool, President and Chief Executive Officer, BorgWarner. “We are proud to foster a culture where employees can thrive while delivering consistent financial performance and advancing our sustainability priorities. We remain focused on positioning BorgWarner for long-term success and creating lasting value for our customers, shareholders and the communities we serve.”

body_text: View All News Savara Announces European and Australian Patent Offices Have Granted Patents for the Liquid Formulation of MOLBREEVI*, Providing Protection in Europe and Australia Until March 2041 July 30, 2026 Download (opens in new window) -- In December 2025, Savara and PARI Were Granted a Joint European Patent Covering the Investigational Drug-Device Combination of MOLBREEVI, Delivered Via PARI’s Proprietary eFlow® Nebulizer System, Through March 2043 -- LANGHORNE, Pa.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Savara Inc. (Nasdaq: SVRA) (the Company), a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on rare respiratory diseases, today announced that the European Patent Office (EPO) has granted a patent covering the liquid formulation of MOLBREEVI, an orally inhaled recombinant human granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF). European patent No.4121000 provides protection for MOLBREEVI through March 2041. Separately, the Australian Patent Office has also granted a patent, No. 62/990,810, covering the liquid formulation of MOLBREEVI, and securing protection in Australia through the same date. “These patents further strengthen the Company’s intellectual property portfolio for MOLBREEVI, providing an additional layer of defense in markets with no approved alternatives,” said Kate McCabe, Chief Legal Officer, Savara. “Together, these patents reflect the strength of our liquid formulation IP across key ex-US markets. In parallel, we are advancing equivalent patent filings in the U.S., including a patent for the drug-device combination, with the aim of securing comprehensive protection across major commercial territories.” MOLBREEVI, delivered via the proprietary eFlow® Nebulizer System, has been granted Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy Designations by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), Orphan Drug Designation by the FDA and by the European Medicines Agency (EMA), and Innovation Passport (IP) and Promising Innovative Medicine (PIM) designations by the U.K.’s Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) for the treatment of autoimmune PAP. About Autoimmune Pulmonary Alveolar Proteinosis (Autoimmune PAP) Autoimmune PAP is a rare lung disease characterized by the abnormal build-up of surfactant in the alveoli of the lungs. Surfactant consists of proteins and lipids and is an important physiological substance that lines the alveoli to prevent them from collapsing. In a healthy lung, excess surfactant is cleared and digested by immune cells called alveolar macrophages. Alveolar macrophages need to be stimulated by granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) to function properly in clearing surfactant, but in autoimmune PAP, GM-CSF is neutralized by antibodies against GM-CSF, rendering macrophages unable to adequately clear surfactant. As a result, an excess of surfactant accumulates in the alveoli, causing impaired gas exchange, resulting in clinical symptoms of shortness of breath, often with cough and frequent fatigue. Patients may also experience episodes of fever, chest pain, or coughing up blood, especially if secondary lung infection develops. In the long term, the disease can lead to serious complications, including lung fibrosis and the need for a lung transplant. About Savara Savara is a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on rare respiratory diseases. Our lead program, MOLBREEVI*, is a recombinant human granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) in Phase 3 development for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (autoimmune PAP). MOLBREEVI is delivered via the proprietary investigational eFlow® Nebulizer System (PARI Pharma GmbH) specifically developed for inhalation of MOLBREEVI. Our management team has significant experience in rare respiratory diseases and pulmonary medicine, identifying unmet needs, and effectively advancing product candidates to approval and commercialization. More information can be found at www.savarapharma.com and LinkedIn. *MOLBREEVI is the proposed trade name for molgramostim inhalation solution. It is not approved in any indication. MOLBREEVI is a trademark of Savara Inc. title: Best Bank Reconciliation Software in 2026: Find the Right Fit Before You Buy
summary: 10 bank reconciliation software platforms reviewed for 2026: match rates, real pricing, and which tool fits your ERP, team size, and invoice volume.
body_text: Your reconciliation platform matches the easy transactions. Your team closes the hard ones manually. That split: how wide it is and how long it takes, is what your month-end close time actually reflects, and it is the one thing most "best of" lists never compare directly. Here are the ten platforms that matter in 2026, evaluated on exactly that. It compares the ten platforms most widely used by finance teams at SaaS companies, mid-market businesses, and enterprises. For each, you will find what it actually does, who it fits, what it costs, and where its limits are, so you can make a decision you will not need to revisit in eighteen months. What Bank Reconciliation Software Actually Does Before comparing platforms, it helps to be precise about what the category solves. Bank reconciliation software connects your bank accounts, ERP, and billing systems, and automatically matches incoming payments against open invoices. When a payment clears, the software applies matching logic in layers: exact reference matches first, then tolerance-based rules for timing or rounding differences, then AI-learned patterns for complex cases like partial payments, grouped payouts, and one-to-many invoice structures. The output is a reconciled ledger with unmatched items queued for human review, an audit-ready transaction log, and real-time visibility into what is still outstanding. The part that most basic tools miss (and most buyers only discover after purchase) is exception management. Every platform in this guide can match a clean transaction. Clean transactions expose nothing about a platform's capability. Edge cases: partial payments, grouped remittances, and multi-invoice payouts are where platforms show what they are actually built to do. That distinction matters more than auto-match rate percentages in most real-world environments. What Separates Strong Reconciliation Software from Weak Narrowing a shortlist is faster when you know which criteria actually predict outcomes. Five factors account for most of the performance variance between platforms. Auto-match rate and matching depth are the most-quoted specifications in the category, and the most misunderstood. Vendor match rates are almost always measured on clean, controlled data. Your AR is not clean. Ask for a proof-of-concept on your actual invoices before trusting any headline number. Also, confirm that the platform handles the edge cases your team sees most: partial payments, grouped payouts, one-to-many invoice relationships, and cross-currency transactions. ERP integration depth determines real-world time savings more than matching accuracy alone. A platform that requires daily exports and imports before matching can significantly offset its accuracy advantages. Verify that the integration is native and two-way: not an API endpoint that requires custom development. Exception management workflow is where daily productivity is won or lost. Weak platforms surface a list. Strong platforms assign exceptions to team members, propose resolutions based on context, track each item through to close, and maintain an audit trail tied to the resolution. The difference between these two experiences is roughly the difference between a three-day close and a seven-day close. Audit trail and compliance controls matter most for companies approaching IPO, subject to SOX, or operating in regulated industries. Look specifically for immutable, timestamped transaction logs, role-based access controls, SOC 2 Type II certification, and export-ready documentation that satisfies external auditors without manual preparation. Time-to-value is the criterion that most evaluation frameworks skip. A platform with 98% matching accuracy that takes eight months to implement delivers less working capital improvement in year one than a platform at 90% that is fully operational in 90 days. Before signing, ask vendors to show you the gap between their average go-live date and the date customers first reported measurable improvement. That gap is the number that determines year-one ROI. With those criteria in mind, here is how the leading platforms compare. 10 Bank Reconciliation Platforms, Compared in One Table 1. Tesorio: Best for SaaS Finance Teams Scaling Order-to-Cash Tesorio is the only platform in this comparison built as a full order-to-cash system rather than a standalone reconciliation tool. Where most platforms stop at matching payments to invoices, Tesorio continues into the collections workflow, the cash application layer, and forward-looking cash flow forecasting: all within a single system. The Cash Application Agent operates at a 90%+ auto-match rate across enterprise ERP environments. The Collections Agent reads AR email threads, extracts payment promises, drafts responses, and escalates accounts showing aging risk before they cross into recovery territory. The AR Forecast generates 13-week rolling cash projections at 95% accuracy. G2 rating: 4.7/5 (235 verified reviews) Best for: B2B SaaS and tech companies at $20M–$500M ARR running NetSuite, Workday, Salesforce, or Sage Intacct. Finance teams that have outgrown their ERP's native AR module and need reconciliation, collections, and forecasting in one place, rather than managing three separate tools. Key features: 90%+ auto-match rate, ML-validated across enterprise ERP environments AI Collections Agent: email triage, payment promise extraction, risk escalation 13-week AR Forecast at 95% accuracy AI-prioritized collector worklists ranked by payment likelihood Native integrations: NetSuite, Workday, Salesforce, Sage Intacct, Stripe #1 for Enterprise AR Implementation on G2, four consecutive quarters (Q1 2026) SOC 2 Type II certified, full audit trail Pricing: Contact sales. Customers typically see measurable ROI within 90 days. What customers see in practice: Veeva Systems cut 90-day-aged AR by 50% and recovered 75% of the team's previously spent time on manual collections after switching from spreadsheet-based prioritization. Smartsheet removed 150,000 customers from spreadsheets entirely and exceeded its quarterly cash collection target by $14 million. Singular Labs handled a 448% surge in invoice volume over three and a half years without adding a single person to the finance team. GitLab reduced manual AR tasks by 30% while maintaining 86% of the current AR across a global customer base. Why it leads to SaaS reconciliation specifically: Subscription billing: monthly cycles, annual prepays, multi-product SKUs, usage-based billing, creates payment patterns that generic platforms regularly mishandle. Tesorio connects natively to both NetSuite and Salesforce, handles monthly and annual billing cycles without custom configuration, and gives AR teams real-time visibility into which accounts are current, which are at risk, and what cash will land in the next 90 days. See Tesorio in action → 2. BlackLine: Best for Enterprise SOX Compliance and Multi-Entity Financial Close BlackLine is the established market leader in enterprise financial close automation. Its account reconciliation module handles templates, approval routing, compliance documentation, and workflow management for organizations with complex entity structures and regulatory obligations. Auto-match rates reach 97–99% on its AI-powered matching modules. The platform integrates with SAP, Oracle, Workday, and other enterprise ERPs, and its audit trail architecture is purpose-built for SOX-compliant environments. Best for: Public companies, pre-IPO organizations building audit readiness, and large enterprises where SOX compliance and multi-entity reconciliation are non-negotiable requirements. Key features: 97–99% auto-match rate (BlackLine 2025 benchmarking report) Automated reconciliation templates with configurable approval workflows SAP, Oracle, Workday integration at enterprise depth Immutable audit trails, SOX-ready control documentation Variance analysis and certification dashboards Multi-entity, multi-currency reconciliation at enterprise scale Pricing: Averages approximately $77,000 per year as of Q1 2026 (Vendr software pricing database). Contracts range from under $20,000 to over $340,000, depending on entity count and modules. For companies under $50M ARR, the cost-to-benefit ratio is typically unfavorable. 3. FloQast: Best for Accounting Teams Managing Month-End Close Workflows FloQast approaches reconciliation from the close management angle. Rather than a transaction matching engine first, it is a workflow coordination tool with reconciliation embedded: organizing who does what, tracking status, routing approvals, and managing checklists, with a matching module that handles common reconciliation use cases. Best for: Companies at $25M–$200M ARR where the primary bottleneck is close coordination and task management rather than high-volume transaction matching or collections automation. Key features: 95–98% auto-match on structured data within the reconciliation module Checklist management and task assignment for close workflows Deadline tracking and approval routing across the accounting team ERP integration with NetSuite, Sage Intacct, QuickBooks, and others Faster implementation than enterprise alternatives UX designed for accountant adoption, not AR specialist workflows Pricing: Generally $40,000–$80,000 per year for mid-market companies, per Numeric.io's pricing guide (March 2026). Note: FloQast's strength is close coordination. Teams that need high-volume AR collections automation or order-to-cash workflow management alongside reconciliation will need a complementary platform. 4. HighRadius: Best for Large Enterprise AR Automation at Scale HighRadius offers a comprehensive financial close and reconciliation suite combining transaction matching, AI-driven close management, and AR automation covering credit, collections, and deductions. It is designed for large enterprise finance operations with the dedicated resources to manage an extended implementation. Best for: Enterprise finance teams at $200M+ ARR with complex AP/AR operations and transaction volumes that justify a three-to-six-month implementation project. Key features: 95% transaction auto-match rate; 90% auto-reconciliation across supported account types (HighRadius product documentation, 2025) AI-powered anomaly detection for exception identification Full AR automation suite: credit, collections, deductions, cash application Integration with SAP, Oracle, Workday, NetSuite Multi-entity, multi-currency reconciliation IDC-recognized treasury and reconciliation platform (2025) Pricing: Custom enterprise pricing. Implementation typically takes three to six months. 5. Numeric: Best for Mid-Market Accounting Teams Replacing Manual Close Processes Numeric is an AI-powered accounting close platform for mid-market finance teams that have outgrown spreadsheets but do not need the cost or complexity of enterprise systems. It focuses on account reconciliation, flux analysis, and close management — designed to be auditor-ready and fast to implement. Best for: Venture-backed and growth-stage companies at $10M–$150M ARR with a dedicated accounting team that needs close automation without a six-month implementation project. Key features: AI-assisted account reconciliation at 90–95% auto-match on structured data Automated flux analysis and variance explanations Month-end close checklists and task management Native integration with NetSuite, QuickBooks, and Xero Audit-ready documentation generated automatically Typical go-live under 30 days Pricing: Generally $30,000–$60,000 per year. Approximately 50% lower than BlackLine for comparable close management functionality, per Numeric's published comparison (2025). Note: Numeric focuses on the accounting close, not AR collections or cash application. Teams that need DSO reduction alongside reconciliation should evaluate other platforms in parallel. 6. ReconArt: Best for High-Volume Dedicated Reconciliation ReconArt is a purpose-built reconciliation platform for organizations with high transaction volumes, complex matching requirements, and a need for dedicated reconciliation infrastructure. It is used primarily by financial services firms, payment processors, and enterprises with specialized requirements that standard close management tools cannot reliably handle. Best for: Finance teams with high daily transaction volumes, complex intercompany reconciliation, or multi-source payment data that exceeds the capability of ERP-native or close management platforms. Key features: 95–98% auto-match across high-volume, multi-source data Configurable matching rules: one-to-many, many-to-many, tolerance-based Intercompany reconciliation across multiple entities Robust audit trail and regulatory reporting ERP integration via API and SFTP Pricing: Starts at approximately $500/month for basic configurations as of Q1 2026. Enterprise tiers are custom-priced by transaction volume and entity count. 7. Trintech: Best for Enterprise Financial Close with Compliance Focus Trintech offers Cadency for large enterprises and Assure for mid-market organizations. Both platforms focus on financial close automation, balance sheet reconciliation, and compliance controls. Trintech competes directly with BlackLine in the enterprise financial close market. Best for: Large organizations with complex close requirements, regulatory obligations, and a need for balance sheet reconciliation at enterprise scale. Key features: 95–99% auto-match on configured reconciliation workflows Balance sheet reconciliation and certification workflows SOX and IFRS compliance controls built into the platform Intercompany reconciliation across large entity structures Risk-based prioritization for high-exposure accounts Integration with SAP, Oracle, Workday Pricing: Custom enterprise pricing, comparable to BlackLine in scope and timeline. 8. Sage Intacct: Best for Mid-Market Teams Already Running Sage For companies already running Sage Intacct, the built-in bank reconciliation module delivers solid performance within the existing environment at no additional cost. There is no separate vendor relationship or integration project required. Best for: Upper mid-market companies at $5M–$100M revenue on Sage Intacct with manageable invoice volume and no immediate requirement for AI collections automation or advanced forecasting. Key features: 88–93% auto-match on bank feeds within the Sage environment Direct GL-to-bank reconciliation without data migration Included in Sage Intacct subscription at no additional cost Clean integration between AP, AR, and bank reconciliation Pricing: Included in the Sage Intacct subscription. Note: Complex matching scenarios, high-volume collections, and cash flow forecasting all require augmentation beyond what Sage's native module provides. Teams outgrowing Sage reconciliation typically move to Tesorio or Numeric for purpose-built automation . 9. Xero: Best for Small Businesses Starting with Reconciliation Automation Xero's JAX (Just Automated Xero) auto-reconciliation feature, launched in beta in November 2025, is designed to handle more than 80% of bank statement lines automatically using transaction pattern learning. It operates within the standard Xero subscription at no additional cost. Best for: Companies generating under $10M annually that need reliable bank-to-book matching without the overhead of a standalone reconciliation platform. Xero handles it within the subscription they are likely already paying for. Key features: 80%+ auto-reconciliation target via JAX (beta, November 2025) Bank feed reconciliation within Xero Continuous match rate improvement through learned transaction rules Included in Xero subscription ($15–$78/month) Pricing: $15–$78/month (Q1 2026). Note: JAX handles simple bank-to-book matching. Multi-entity structures, complex collections, and teams processing thousands of invoices monthly will outgrow Xero's reconciliation capability quickly. 10. QuickBooks Online: Best for Startups and Basic Small Business Reconciliation QuickBooks Online applies suggested match logic to compare bank transactions against your ledger. It is the starting point for most small businesses and is adequate for modest monthly transaction volumes. Best for: Companies under $5M revenue, early-stage startups, and businesses with limited monthly invoice volume that do not yet require a dedicated reconciliation function. Key features: 70–80% auto-match using suggested transaction matching Bank feed reconciliation within QuickBooks Included in QuickBooks Online subscription ($30–$200/month) Familiar interface widely used by bookkeepers and small business accountants Pricing: $30–$200/month (Q1 2026). Note: No AI prioritization, no collections automation, and no cash flow forecasting. Most SaaS companies outgrow QuickBooks' reconciliation capability within 12–18 months of meaningful revenue growth. How AI Is Changing Bank Reconciliation in 2026 Understanding where the category is headed affects which platform you choose today: specifically, whether you invest in a rule-based system with a ceiling or a learning system with room to grow. Traditional reconciliation software matched transactions by rule: if the reference number matches and the amount is within tolerance, approve it. AI-powered platforms match by pattern. They learn from payment history, customer behavior, and timing to handle cases that rules cannot anticipate: partial payments, grouped payouts, remittances with no reference data. Beyond matching, AI has moved into the surrounding workflow. According to Protiviti's September 2025 Global Finance Trends Survey , the share of finance organizations actively using AI tools more than doubled in a single year, reaching close to three-quarters of all finance functions. That adoption is showing up in how the best-performing teams operate: exceptions are prioritized automatically, collections outreach is triggered by the same matching engine that cleared the invoice, and cash positions update in real time rather than at close. McKinsey's research on finance transformation, cited in the Tesorio 2025 AR Benchmark Report , found that companies applying AI to collections and billing workflows are seeing 20–30% improvements in working capital metrics, driven by faster collections and fewer disputes. The practical implication for your buying decision: auto-match rates above 90% are now the baseline expectation for purpose-built platforms. The more useful question to ask any vendor is not how often their platform matches, but what the platform does with every match, every exception, and every resolved payment in terms of improving what comes next. Platforms that use matching data to feed collections prioritization, cash forecasting, and exception resolution are building a compounding advantage. Platforms that stop at matching are building a ceiling. What to Watch Out For: Common Limitations Across the Category Reconciliation software adds significant value when it fits. It adds cost and friction when it does not. Each of the following issues surfaces regularly in post-implementation reviews, and almost none of them come up during vendor demos. Headline auto-match rates that do not reflect your data. Vendors typically measure match rates on clean, well-structured datasets. Your actual data, with partial payments, deduction codes, and remittances missing reference numbers, will produce a different number. Ask every vendor to run a proof-of-concept on a sample of your real transactions before signing. ERP version compatibility gaps. Many platforms advertise integration with NetSuite or SAP. The integration quality varies significantly by ERP version and module configuration. Always verify compatibility against your specific version, not just the ERP brand name. Implementation timelines that slip. Enterprise platforms routinely quote four-to-six-week implementation timelines and take three to six months in practice. Request references from recent customers and ask specifically for median time-to-first-value, not best-case examples. Adoption friction on lean teams. Platforms designed for large AR departments with dedicated specialists can be difficult to adopt for a two- or three-person team. Tesorio and Numeric both offer faster onboarding models suited for leaner finance structures. BlackLine and HighRadius are not the right fit until organizational complexity justifies their implementation requirements. Reconciliation treated as isolated from collections. This is the most common structural mistake. A platform that stops at matching leaves the collections workflow in a separate system or in spreadsheets. For SaaS companies where collections is the primary DSO lever, keeping reconciliation isolated from AR management erodes the efficiency gains from automation and keeps the month-end close a manual event. What a Good Month-End Reconciliation Process Looks Like Understanding these limitations naturally leads to the next question: What does a well-run reconciliation process look like with the right software in place? Here is what that continuous process looks like in practice: This cadence is only possible when the reconciliation platform feeds the collections workflow : when matching a payment automatically updates the collections priority queue, and when a customer's payment promise logged by the Collections Agent is visible to the person running the close. That connection is what distinguishes a reconciliation platform from a reconciliation tool. From Comparison to Decision: Where to Go From Here Every platform in this guide crosses 90% on clean data. The question is what happens to the other 10%. A platform that returns a list of unmatched exceptions and stops is a reconciliation tool. A platform that assigns exceptions to owners, proposes resolutions based on context, routes payment promises back to the collector's queue, and updates the cash forecast before the close window closes is a reconciliation system. That gap is wider than any match rate number in this guide. The evaluation sequence follows directly from that distinction. Require every vendor to demo exception management on your actual data. Confirm that ERP integration is native and two-way. Ask for the median time-to-first-value from reference customers at your company size. Those three questions separate platforms that perform on clean demos from platforms that hold up in production. Finance teams that have made this shift describe a consistent set of changes in their operations: fewer exceptions sitting unresolved past close, cleaner handoffs between matching and collections follow-up, and less manual cleanup before the Monday AR review. Across 200+ verified G2 reviews , that pattern holds across company sizes and ERP environments. If you are ready to test it against your own environment, three starting points: Interactive Product Demo : Watch what happens when a partial payment arrives with no reference number: specifically, how the exception is surfaced, assigned, resolved, and fed back to the collections workflow. That sequence is where platforms diverge most from each other. Book a Call : Bring your ERP version, monthly invoice volume, current exception rate, and the close-week scenarios that consume the most manual time. That is the conversation that determines whether the platform actually fits your environment. ROI Calculator : Plug in your current DSO and AR volume. See what a 15- or 33-day improvement means in working capital: that is the number to bring into the budget conversation before any vendor call starts. Once reconciliation feeds the collections workflow rather than sitting beside it, close time and DSO tend to move together. Frequently Asked Questions What is the best bank reconciliation software for SaaS companies? For SaaS and tech finance teams at $20M–$500M ARR, Tesorio is the most purpose-built option. It connects bank reconciliation to collections, cash application, and AR forecasting in one platform, handles subscription billing cycles natively, and integrates with NetSuite and Salesforce. Customers average a 33-day DSO reduction. What is a good auto-match rate for reconciliation software? Match rates below 85% leave too many exceptions to generate meaningful time savings. Purpose-built platforms operate between 90% and 99%. The practical difference between 90% and 98% matching on 2,000 monthly transactions is roughly 160 fewer items requiring manual review each month. How does bank reconciliation software reduce DSO? Reconciliation automation reduces DSO by eliminating the lag between payment receipt and invoice matching. When payments are applied same-day rather than in weekly batches, the open AR balance reflects the actual cash position rather than the processing delay. Combined with AI collections prioritization, automated platforms consistently reduce DSO by 15–33 days for SaaS companies. How long does implementation take? Cloud-native platforms with pre-built ERP connectors typically go live in weeks. Tesorio customers reach full operational impact within 90 days. Numeric targets sub-30-day go-lives for mid-market teams. Enterprise platforms like BlackLine and HighRadius typically take three to six months. Free Guide How Big Should My AR Team Be?
